title: 35.8 DustNet: A Network of Time-Division Multiplexed Ultrasonic Implants with 16-Level ASK Backscatter Modulation
problem: Multi-implant wireless neural recording networks require simultaneous data rates of 200-400kb/s from 4-8 distributed implants at depths of several cm with minimal infection risk, exceeding capabilities of existing RF/optical approaches.
motivation: Real-time distributed neural signal recording (LFP, AP, EMG) from multiple implants enables motor control in prosthetics and nerve-damage recovery, but RF and optical methods suffer from shallow penetration or low data rates.
method: DustNet uses ultrasound—sound frequencies around 1-9 MHz that pass through body tissue without getting absorbed—to send data to and from tiny implants placed several centimeters deep. Each implant takes its turn transmitting (time-division multiplexing) so they don't interfere with each other. When receiving, implants send data back by reflecting the ultrasound at one of 16 different signal strengths (16-level ASK backscatter modulation), allowing each implant to transmit at 50kb/s.
key_novelty: DustNet achieves multi-implant wireless neural recording at clinical tissue depths using ultrasound implants with time-division multiplexing (taking turns) and 16-level signal strength modulation (16-level ASK backscatter).
contributions: TDM ultrasonic scheme for coordinating multi-implant communication
16-level ASK backscatter modulation maximizing bandwidth utilization
Achievement of 200-400kb/s aggregate data rate across 4-8 implants at cm-scale depths
primary_theme: Ultrasonic TDM neural implant network with backscatter communication
